question: Do our researchers' co-authors have more co-authors than they do?
headline: 93.2% of researchers have fewer co-authors than their co-authors do. The average researcher has 9.1 co-authors, but the average co-author has 30.8.
method_note: Computed on the co-authorship largest connected component (7,752 researchers; papers with >30 listed authors dropped). Neighbor degree is the unweighted average degree of all direct co-authors.
